status: all four selected benign captures and the first Mirai split audited in full; benign passes the direction gate, Mirai fails it, and no model has read any capture.
what_changed_since_12_september: The 12 September audit recorded cicresearch.ca as unreachable and therefore audited nothing. On 22 September the host answered from the shell with the proxy unset. Long transfers are throttled and dropped, and the server rejects Range requests. On 27 September a systemd-inhibited download loop was still fetching additional, non-selected folder splits.

findings: The victim list identifies devices by model name and MAC address across 43 pages and carries no IP address or CIDR anywhere. Neither does the PCAP readme.
Device identity therefore cannot be declared from the dataset's documentation. It has to be derived from the capture itself by mapping Ethernet source MAC to IP, and any result must say so.
Captures are split by tcpdump into files of at most 2 GB, so one attack class spans several files.

audited.lan_source: observed: 455,776 of the sampled private addresses fall in this /24 and nothing else comes close. The documentation carries no addresses at all.
audited.top_pairs_note: the heaviest flows are device to public address (35.185.101.66 and 74.125.0.107 are Google ranges, 157.249.81.141 is external); the heaviest LOCAL pair is 192.168.137.172 to .58
audited.supersedes_prefix_audit: the 20 MB prefix audited on 23 September at 00:43 gave 45.5 % EGRESS; the full file gives 47.6 %, and LOCAL falls from 20.6 % to 12.6 %

reading.benign_traffic_is_egress_dominant: 47.6 % of 3.55 million IP packets leave the LAN, against 78 % (4-1), 46 % (7-1) and 35 % (5-1) for the IoT-23 benign captures. This source matches the egress threat model as well as the data we already use.
reading.it_answers_the_weakness_KAN_52_exposed: One capture carries 68 distinct devices over 9.26 hours. Every benign figure in the project so far rests on a single honeypot, and the KAN-52 test confirmation showed that a zero there can come from one capture’s gap structure rather than from the detector.
what_this_does_not_say: It says nothing about the attack captures. ADR-0004’s topology concern is about attacks between IoT devices, and the Mirai capture is still not downloaded.
Device identity rests on MAC-to-IP observed in the capture; the published documentation carries no addresses.
A capture holding 68 devices does not fit the one-device-per-capture assumption the current runners make. Per-device windows would have to be built and declared before any scoring.
Nothing here adopts the source. ADR-0004 stays PROPOSED and the G1 choice stays formally in force.

next: use the benign captures only after the per-device MAC-to-IP grouping and capture-aware split contract is reviewed
do not use the selected Mirai capture for an egress transfer claim because 98.52 % of its IP packets are LOCAL
keep every additionally downloaded folder outside the experiment until it has a separately frozen selection and role

audited_second.note: a second, independent file gives the same answer as the first, so the egress share is not a sampling accident

audited_mirai.gate: rejected for the egress transfer test: LOCAL dominates and EGRESS is below one percent

conclusion.benign: All four selected benign splits are EGRESS-dominant at 47.6-50.3 percent and carry 65-68 observed LAN source MACs. They are suitable candidates for the new-device benign evaluation after a reviewed per-device grouping and capture-aware split is frozen.
conclusion.malware: The selected Mirai split is 98.52 percent LOCAL and therefore cannot support an OmniGuard gateway-egress detection claim.
conclusion.model_use: No capture was used for fitting, threshold selection, policy selection or scoring. The published CSV archive remains forbidden as a model input.
